m:meta.m:name: KoSIT Validator Specification
m:meta.m:abstract: Semantic model of the KoSIT Validator Specification: the conformance validation report (CVR structure cvr) and the scenario configuration (structure scenario, placeholder)

m:description.m:p: One model, two structures. CVR is the conformance validation report the validator emits; scenario is the configuration it is driven by. Both share the datatypes and the definitions below. The scenario structure is a placeholder until the working session of week 37/2026; its terms (BG-14, BT-44, BT-45) are the starting point, not a decision.

This model describes the conformance validation report (CVR) semantically: which information a report carries, how it is composed into a message, which constraints hold, and how it maps to the concrete syntax. That syntax is CVR — a profile of XVRL (http://www.xproc.org/ns/xvrl) with its own namespace (urn:conformatron:cvr:draft).

The CV Report is organized by validation actions: every executed action of the canonical pipeline produces exactly one report. Action names are not free text — they are the action types of the validator's API module (CTActionType).

Term names deliberately follow the vocabulary of the serialized report (reports, creator, detection, context, digest, …), so a reader of a CVR instance can find the corresponding business term without a translation table.

Identifier scheme: BT-n for terms, BG-n for groups of terms, BR-CVR-n for rules. Rules that the CVR Schematron (validator/cvr/src/main/resources/sch/cvr-1.0.sch) checks carry their assert-ids; the rules without one are the open decisions and the constraints no Schematron can see (engine behaviour, verbosity modes).

Sources of this model: the report specification (content/en/docs/specifications/conformance-validation-report-spec.md), the annotated reference instance (validator/e2e/prime-example.xml), the CvrWriter serializer of the reference implementation, and the enumerations of the validator's API module (CTActionType, CTStandardValidationType, CTConformanceResult, CTDecision).

m:requirement-group.m:name: Report
m:requirement-group.m:description: Requirements pertaining to the validation/conformance report.

m:requirement-group.m:name: Configuration Requirements
m:requirement-group.m:description: Requirements pertaining to configuration of a validation.

m:requirement.m:description: scenario config is as close as possible to old one (or we have determistic upgrader)
capapble of checking xml declaration and declared encoding
Allow for checking allowed character sets
A report has to hold up in audit scenarios: the document under examination is contained unchanged or at least referenced resolvably, and every artifact validated against is provable by a hash.

Verbosity of the report has to be customizable (audit/full as the default, compact, digest, acceptable). A mode is only allowed to omit information from the full report, never to change the structure.
The report has to represent cancelled runs: a partial report covering the actions executed so far is always serializable.
Additional reports have to be addable for downstream processes.

m:datatype.m:name: Any
m:datatype.m:description: Ur-type. Base of all other datatypes.

m:datatype.m:name: Binary
m:datatype.m:description: A finite sequence of binary digits.

m:datatype.m:name: Code
m:datatype.m:description: A value from a fixed enumerated value space. The actual allowed value space is declared in term definitions using codelist element.

m:datatype.m:name: Date Time
m:datatype.m:description: A point in time with date, time of day and time zone.

m:notes.m:usage-note: Serialized as xs:dateTime. The time zone is mandatory and the seconds component must be written out — a serialization that drops the seconds when they are zero is not a valid xs:dateTime.

m:datatype.m:name: Embedded Content
m:datatype.m:description: A complete document embedded into the report — either as an element tree (readable) or base64-encoded (byte-faithful) string. The kind of embedding is always stated explicitly.

m:datatype.m:name: Hash Value
m:datatype.m:description: The value of a cryptographic digest, in hexadecimal notation.

m:datatype.m:name: Identifier
m:datatype.m:description: An identifier that names a subject unambiguously within a known context.

m:datatype.m:name: Group
m:datatype.m:description: Container for related terms. Carries no value of its own.

m:datatype.m:name: Text
m:datatype.m:description: Free-form text intended for human readers.

m:datatype.m:name: URI
m:datatype.m:description: A Uniform Resource Identifier pointing at a document or a validation artifact.

m:datatype.m:name: XPath Expression
m:datatype.m:description: An XPath expression denoting a location in an XML document.

m:codelist.m:name: Run Status
m:codelist.m:description: Whether the pipeline ran to completion or was cancelled. Allowed values: COMPLETED, CANCELLED.

m:codelist.m:name: Action Name
m:codelist.m:description: The canonical validation actions. Values: detect-syntax, parse-document, detect-scenarios, select-scenario, retrieve-artifacts, prepare-rules, apply-rules, compute-conformance, decision-recommendation. The value space is the CTActionType enumeration of the validator's API module.

m:codelist.m:name: Severity
m:codelist.m:description: The severity of a detection as defined by XVRL. Values: info, warning, error, fatal-error, unspecified.

m:codelist.m:name: Conformance Result
m:codelist.m:description: The outcome of the conformance computation for one conformance target. Values: CONFORMANT, NON_CONFORMANT, INCONCLUSIVE (CTConformanceResult).

m:codelist.m:name: Decision
m:codelist.m:description: The recommendation to the calling process. Values: ACCEPT,REJECT, EVALUATE_FURTHER (CTDecision).

m:codelist.m:name: Encoding
m:codelist.m:description: How an embedded document is encoded in the report. Values: dom (element tree, readable), base64 (byte-faithful). The value space is deliberately open for extension, e.g. gzip+base64 for large source documents.

m:codelist.m:name: Schema Type Namespace
m:codelist.m:description: The namespace of the language a rule set is written in. Values: http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema, http://purl.oclc.org/dsdl/schematron. XVRL states the schema language via schematypens; there is no language attribute.

m:codelist.m:name: Artifact Type
m:codelist.m:description: The kind of a validation artifact, e.g. xsd, partial-xsd, schematron-xslt2, schematron-schxslt2-xslt3. The value space is the CTStandardValidationType enumeration of the validator's API module; it distinguishes compiler and target XSLT version because the validation outcome depends on them.

m:codelist.m:name: Hash Algorithm
m:codelist.m:description: The algorithm a digest was computed with, currently SHA-512. The algorithm is exchangeable and is therefore always carried alongside the value instead of being encoded in a property name.

m:codelist.m:name: Supplemental Role
m:codelist.m:description: What a supplemental serves for, currently java-trace for the technical call path of an engine error.

m:codelist.m:name: Media Type
m:codelist.m:description: The media type of an embedded document.

m:codelist.m:name: Character Set
m:codelist.m:description: The character encoding of a source document.

m:term.m:name: Conformance Validation Report
m:term.m:description: The complete report on one validation run: the conformance statement about the document under examination, the metadata of the run, and detailed (sub)reports per executed action.

m:term.m:name: Conformant
m:term.m:description: Whether the document under examination is conformant overall. This is distinct from common validation outcomes: configured severity overrides can make a document conformant even though a rule set reports findings (e.g. errors).

m:term.m:name: Run Status
m:term.m:description: Whether the pipeline ran to completion or was cancelled. A cancelled run yields a partial report containing exactly the actions that were executed before cancellation.

m:term.m:name: Run Metadata
m:term.m:description: Information items to describe the whole validation run: when it was serialized, which validator produced it and which document was examined.

m:term.m:name: Report Timestamp
m:term.m:description: The point in time the report was produced.

m:term.m:name: Validator Name
m:term.m:description: The software that performed the validation run.

m:term.m:name: Validator Version
m:term.m:description: The version of that software. Together with the name it supports reproducible validation runs.

m:term.m:name: Document Reference
m:term.m:description: Reference to the document under examination. It has to be resolvable within the scope of further processing and storing the report.

m:term.m:name: Run Identifier
m:term.m:description: An identifier unique across runs, by which a report can be addressed in downstream processes.

m:term.m:name: Action Report
m:term.m:description: The report on exactly one executed action of the pipeline. An action that applies several rule sets produces one action report per rule set.

m:term.m:name: Action Metadata
m:term.m:description: Identity of the action: which action, when, with which engine and against which rule set.

m:term.m:name: Creator Name
m:term.m:description: The name of the executed action. It is the identity of the action report.

m:term.m:name: Action Timestamp
m:term.m:description: The point in time associated with the action.

m:notes.m:note: Currently the serialization time. Real per-action execution times (start and duration) require an execution record in the API.

m:term.m:name: Engine Name
m:term.m:description: The technical component the action employed, e.g. the XSLT processor or the Schematron transpiler.

m:term.m:name: Engine Version
m:term.m:description: The version of that component. For Schematron it co-determines the validation outcome and is therefore part of the evidence.

m:term.m:name: Applied Schema
m:term.m:description: The rule set the action validated against, with its language and the parameters it was applied under.

m:term.m:name: Schema Reference
m:term.m:description: Reference to the applied rule set.

m:term.m:name: Schema Type Namespace
m:term.m:description: The language of the rule set, given as a namespace.

m:term.m:name: Schematron Phase
m:term.m:description: The phase of a Schematron rule set that was executed. Running only a selected phase changes the validation outcome, so the phase is part of the record.

m:term.m:name: Detection
m:term.m:description: A single observation made by the action — a rule finding, an intermediate observation, or evidence such as the embedded document under examination. Every failure path emits a detection, which is what keeps a cancelled run reportable.

m:term.m:name: Severity
m:term.m:description: The severity of the detection.

m:term.m:name: Original Severity
m:term.m:description: The severity the rule set itself assigned, where the configuration overrides it. It makes the override auditable instead of silently replacing the original.

m:term.m:name: Detection Code
m:term.m:description: The identifier of the rule that produced the detection.

m:term.m:name: Scenario Identifier
m:term.m:description: The identifier of the validation scenario the detection is about.

m:notes.m:note: The target is a coordinate of the conformance target. As long as the scenario configuration carries no identifier, the scenario name is used.

m:term.m:name: Artifact Identifier
m:term.m:description: The identifier of the validation artifact the detection is about. On failures this is the decisive information — which artifact is missing or unreadable.

m:term.m:name: Target Identifier
m:term.m:description: The identifier of the conformance target whose conformance is being stated.

m:term.m:name: Conformance Result
m:term.m:description: The outcome of the conformance computation for one conformance target. A rule set that was never executed counts as non-conformant — not executed must not look like conformant.

m:term.m:name: Detection Context
m:term.m:description: The subject a detection is about: where it is located and which digest identifies it.

m:term.m:name: Location
m:term.m:description: The place the detection was made at — in a document or in a configuration file.

m:term.m:name: Location XPath
m:term.m:description: The location as an XPath expression. XPath is stable across serializations and line numbers are not, which makes XPath the primary location information.

m:term.m:name: Location Line
m:term.m:description: The line of the location, where the engine supplies it.

m:term.m:name: Location Column
m:term.m:description: The column of the location, where the engine supplies it.

m:term.m:name: Location Reference
m:term.m:description: Reference to the file the location is in.

m:term.m:name: Artifact Type
m:term.m:description: The kind of artifact at the location.

m:term.m:name: Hash
m:term.m:description: The cryptographic digest of the subject the detection is about. It is what makes the report provable: without it nothing shows which version of a rule set the validation ran against.

m:term.m:name: Hash Algorithm
m:term.m:description: The algorithm the digest was computed with.

m:term.m:name: Hash Value
m:term.m:description: The value of the digest.

m:term.m:name: Message
m:term.m:description: A statement made by the detection — as text for human readers, or as an embedded document serving as evidence.

m:term.m:name: Message Identifier
m:term.m:description: A stable identifier of the message. It allows addressing one particular message without relying on document order.

m:term.m:name: Media Type
m:term.m:description: The media type of the embedded document.

m:term.m:name: Encoding
m:term.m:description: The encoding of the embedded document.

m:term.m:name: Source Encoding
m:term.m:description: The character encoding the source document declared. With base64 embedding it is needed to write the original back out; with tree embedding it is the evidence that tree embedding was permissible.

m:term.m:name: Message Text
m:term.m:description: The statement of the detection in human-readable form.

m:term.m:name: Embedded Document
m:term.m:description: The document backing the detection — the document under examination itself, or the selected validation scenario.

m:term.m:name: Supplement
m:term.m:description: Technical additions to a detection that are needed for diagnosis but are not part of its substantive statement.

m:term.m:name: Supplement Role
m:term.m:description: Purpose of supplemental.

m:term.m:name: Supplement Content
m:term.m:description: The content, e.g. the technical call path of an engine error.

m:term.m:name: Digest
m:term.m:description: The condensation of an action report. It holds only information derivable from the detections and is meant for readers who do not evaluate every detection.

m:term.m:name: Digest Valid
m:term.m:description: Whether the action was successful.

m:term.m:name: Worst Severity
m:term.m:description: The highest severity that occurred in this action.

m:term.m:name: Error Count
m:term.m:description: The number of detections with severity error.

m:term.m:name: Warning Count
m:term.m:description: The number of detections with severity warning.

m:term.m:name: Error Code
m:term.m:description: The identifier of a rule that produced an error in this action. The set of these identifiers allows an assessment without reading the detections.

m:term.m:name: Decision Recommendation
m:term.m:description: The recommendation to the calling process on what to do with the document under examination, together with its rationale.

m:notes.m:note: The terminal action. It always runs — also for a cancelled run, which it rejects naming the cancelling action — so every report ends in an explicit verdict.

m:term.m:name: Decision
m:term.m:description: The recommended decision about the document under examination.

m:term.m:name: Decision Summary
m:term.m:description: Why the decision comes out the way it does.

m:term.m:name: Scenario
m:term.m:description: Placeholder. One scenario description: the rule that says when the scenario is responsible for a document, plus the validation artifacts a recognized document is validated with.

m:notes.m:note: Placeholder. Today's configuration (framework/2/scenarios) knows scenario, name, description, namespace, match, validateWithXmlSchema, validateWithSchematron, createReport with customLevel, acceptMatch and noScenarioReport on collection level. Version 2 has to add at least a scenario identifier as a coordinate, the separation of syntax and rule sets, conformance targets per rule set and the move of the assessment out of the report XSLT into the pipeline. None of this is modelled yet.

m:term.m:name: Scenario Name
m:term.m:description: Placeholder. The name of the scenario; today at the same time its identifier, because the configuration carries no id of its own.

m:term.m:name: Match Expression
m:term.m:description: Placeholder. The XPath expression evaluated against the document under examination; true means the scenario is responsible.

m:rule-group.m:name: Structure Rules
m:rule-group.m:description: Constraints on the organization and completeness of the report.

m:rule-group.m:name: Identity Rules
m:rule-group.m:description: Constraints on the provability of the document and the validation artifacts.

m:rule-group.m:name: Severity Rules
m:rule-group.m:description: Constraints on severities and their configured override.

m:rule-group.m:name: Embedding Rules
m:rule-group.m:description: Constraints on embedding documents into the report.

m:rule-group.m:name: Open Decisions
m:rule-group.m:description: Constraints still to be decided. They are recorded here so they are not lost, and they do not bind yet.

m:rule.m:name: A CVR is a profile of XVRL
m:rule.m:description: A conformance validation report shall validate against XVRL.

m:rule.m:name: Extensions live in the CVR namespace
m:rule.m:description: Every piece of information XVRL does not define shall be expressed in the CVR extension namespace.

m:rule.m:name: One action report per executed action
m:rule.m:description: The report shall be organized by action: exactly one action report per executed action, in execution order. An action that applies several rule sets shall produce one action report per rule set.

m:rule.m:name: Creator name from the value space
m:rule.m:description: Every action report shall name exactly one creator, and that name shall come from the value space of canonical action names.

m:rule.m:name: Digest always present and last
m:rule.m:description: Every action report shall contain exactly one digest, and it shall be the last child of the action report.

m:rule.m:name: Partial report on cancellation
m:rule.m:description: The report shall always carry the conformance statement and the run status. A cancelled run shall yield a partial report containing exactly the executed actions and shall remain serializable.

m:rule.m:name: Every failure path emits a detection
m:rule.m:description: A failed action shall still yield report content. No information may exist only in logs or in local state.

m:rule.m:name: No detection code without own identity
m:rule.m:description: A detection shall carry a detection code only where it has an identity of its own — a rule finding or an error. Otherwise the creator name of the action report already says what the detection is about, and a second code would be redundant.

m:rule.m:name: Severity only where it carries meaning
m:rule.m:description: A detection shall carry a severity where the severity says something. A detection in the error band shall always carry it — otherwise a detection without severity would stand next to a non-zero error count in the digest.

m:rule.m:name: An overridden severity is auditable
m:rule.m:description: Where the configuration assigns a rule a severity other than the one the rule set assigns, the detection shall carry the effective severity and additionally the original severity. The override works in both directions — raising and lowering.

m:rule.m:name: Engine errors are not overridable
m:rule.m:description: The severity of a detection originating in an error of the validation engine itself shall not be configurable. A run that failed technically must not be made to look harmless by configuration.

m:rule.m:name: Document reference in every verbosity mode
m:rule.m:description: In every verbosity mode the report shall contain at least a reference to the document under examination that is resolvable within the scope of further processing and storing the report.

m:rule.m:name: Document identity on parse
m:rule.m:description: The action that reads the document shall state its digest together with the algorithm name — including where the document is not well-formed. The report can then always identify the document.

m:rule.m:name: Artifact identity
m:rule.m:description: Every retrieved validation artifact shall be named, located and — where its bytes were read — fingerprinted with a digest.

m:rule.m:name: Applied schema states its language
m:rule.m:description: An applied rule set shall always be stated together with its schema type namespace.

m:rule.m:name: Embed only well-formed XML
m:rule.m:description: The document under examination shall be embedded only where it is well-formed XML. Otherwise the report shall contain the reference alone.

m:rule.m:name: Originality over readability
m:rule.m:description: An XML document in UTF-8 shall be embedded as an element tree; any other character encoding and any non-XML syntax shall be embedded base64-encoded, stating the source encoding. Rationale: with tree embedding the fragment is converted into the encoding of the surrounding document and is no longer byte-faithfully reproducible. The kind of embedding shall not be configurable.

m:rule.m:name: An embedded document is addressable
m:rule.m:description: Every message that embeds a document shall carry a stable message identifier. Access must not rely on the order of messages.

m:rule.m:name: Only the selected scenario
m:rule.m:description: The action that selects a validation scenario shall embed that single scenario as-is — not the collection and not the whole configuration.

m:rule.m:name: Condensation only removes
m:rule.m:description: A lower verbosity mode shall only omit information. The structure of the report shall stay the same in every mode.

m:rule.m:name: The digest is derivable
m:rule.m:description: The digest shall contain only statements derivable from the detections of the action. It is condensation, not additional information.

m:rule.m:name: No XInclude in the embedded scenario
m:rule.m:description: A validation scenario shall not contain XInclude, so that the embedded scenario is the one actually applied. The check would have to happen in the code.
Open: proposed as a decision, not yet taken.

m:rule.m:name: Normalization before digest computation
m:rule.m:description: How an artifact is normalized before its digest is computed has to be settled so that digests are comparable across platforms — in particular the treatment of line endings and trailing white-space.
Open: the need is recognized, the decision is outstanding.

m:rule.m:name: Several engines per action
m:rule.m:description: An action can employ several technical components — a transpiler and an XSLT processor, for instance. Where those are stated when there is more than one has to be settled.
Open: XVRL permits only one validator at this position.

m:rule.m:name: Executed versus finding-free
m:rule.m:description: An action report without detections is indistinguishable from an action that never ran. Whether the digest needs an explicit executed property has to be settled.
Open: arose from dropping the code for a finding-free rule set application.

m:structure.m:name: Conformance Validation Report
m:structure.m:description: The composition of the report: one validation run with metadata, any number of action reports and an optional decision recommendation.

m:structure.m:name: Scenario Configuration
m:structure.m:description: Placeholder for the composition of the scenario configuration (version 2, to be modelled in week 37/2026).

m:notes.m:note: Serialized as a whitespace-separated list of identifiers in one attribute.
